biography.value:
Background

Morgash the Gravemaker was born in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate and earned his surname digging graves for the poor before he ever swung a sword for coin. He enlisted with the Flaming Fist and was on the walls the day the mind flayers came — when the netherbrain rose from the harbor and the sky over the Gate filled with nautiloids, Morgash held a barricade on the Basilisk Gate with a company that started forty strong and ended the battle at nine. In the chaos of those weeks he fought beside a githyanki warrioress named Lae'zel, fierce and exacting, and what began as trading insults over a whetstone became a romance — brief, blazing, and the realest thing he took from the war. When the city was saved she told him plainly: her destiny lay in the Astral Plane, in a war for her people's freedom, and no mortal city could hold her. She flew to it without looking back, and Morgash — who had buried half his company that season — found the Gate too full of ghosts to stay.

He drifted north up the Trade Way and settled in Daggerford, hiring out his blade to caravans and telling no one why an orc veteran drinks alone on the anniversary of the battle. It was there he first heard the story of the Broken Heart — a relic shattered into four shards and scattered through the Misty Woods far to the south — and the name alone hooked into him like a barbed arrow. He tells the others it's about the prize; a relic like that could buy a mercenary's retirement ten times over. But some quiet part of Morgash believes that a heart broken into pieces can be gathered up and made whole again — and he needs that to be true.

Potion, Common

You regain 2d4 + 2 Hit Points when you drink this potion.

Whatever its potency, the potion’s red liquid glimmers when agitated.
A Backpack holds up to 30 pounds within 1 cubic foot. It can also serve as a saddlebag.

A bedroll sleeps one Small or Medium creature. Bundled snug in its quilted layers, a sleeper can pass even a bitterly cold night unharmed — travelers swear no chill has ever bitten through a well-made bedroll.
Rations consist of travel-ready food, including jerky, dried fruit, hardtack, and nuts. See &Reference[Malnutrition] in the rules glossary for the risks of not eating.

A Torch burns for 1 hour, casting Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet. When you take the Attack action, you can attack with the Torch, using it as a Simple Melee weapon. On a hit, the target takes 1 Fire damage.

As a Utilize action, you can tie a knot with Rope if you succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check. The Rope can be burst with a successful DC 20 Strength (Athletics) check.

You can bind an unwilling creature with the Rope only if the creature has the &Reference[Grappled], &Reference[Incapacitated], or &Reference[Restrained] condition. If the creature’s legs are bound, the creature has the Restrained condition until it escapes. Escaping the Rope requires the creature to make a successful DC 15 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check as an action.

A Tinderbox is a small container holding flint, fire steel, and tinder (usually dry cloth soaked in light oil) used to kindle a fire. Using it to light a Candle, Lamp, Lantern, or Torch—or anything else with exposed fuel—takes a Bonus Action. Lighting any other fire takes 1 minute.
A Waterskin holds up to 4 pints. If you don’t drink sufficient water, you risk &Reference[dehydration].
A Healer’s Kit has ten uses. As a Utilize action, you can expend one of its uses to stabilize an Unconscious creature that has 0 Hit Points without needing to make a Wisdom (Medicine) check.

(Prerequisite: Fighting Style Feature)

When you roll damage for an attack you make with a Melee weapon that you are holding with two hands, you can treat any 1 or 2 on a damage die as a 3. The weapon must have the Two-Handed or Versatile property to gain this benefit.

Foundry Note

This effect is not automated.

A tarnished badge of the Flaming Fist of Baldur's Gate — a mailed gauntlet wreathed in flame. The pin is bent from being torn off and pinned back on more than once. Along the Sword Coast, veterans who show it still get a nod, a drink, and sometimes a job.

items.name: Campaign Coin — the Battle of Baldur's Gate

description.value:
A thick bronze coin struck for the defenders of Baldur's Gate — the ones who held when the nautiloids darkened the sky and the netherbrain rose from the harbor. The obverse shows the Basilisk Gate, standing. The reverse has been scratched over with a knife-point: thirty-one names in a gravedigger's careful column, every one crossed out.

He dug every one of those graves himself.

A sword-belt buckle of strange silvery metal, angular in the fashion of no smith of this world — githyanki work, to an eye that has seen it before. It is kept polished to a mirror shine, though the belt it matched is long gone to the Astral Plane, and the hands that wore it with it.

It is not for sale. It has never been for sale.

Wondrous Item, Uncommon

A parting gift from a temple infirmarian in Daggerford who judged the party “the sort who’ll need it sooner than most.” The jar has been resealed with wax more times than it has doses left.

This glass jar, 3 inches in diameter, contains 1d4 + 1 doses of a thick mixture that smells faintly of aloe. The jar and its contents weigh 1/2 pound.

As a Utilize action, you can swallow one dose of the ointment or apply it to a creature within 5 feet of yourself. The creature that receives it regains 2d8 + 2 Hit Points and ceases to have the &Reference[Poisoned apply=false] condition.

Foundry Note

The Determine Doses activity is provided for optional use and will consume item uses to produce a total of 1d4 + 1 remaining uses as described above. Once the number of doses has been determined, that activity may be deleted.

The Use Ointment activity can be used for the healing roll but it does not automatically end the Poisoned condition.
A little cask of good wine, still sealed and sloshing — the raiders were saving it for later.

Weapon (Maul), Rare (Requires Attunement)

This weighty maul's head is etched with spiraling grooves that seem to pull it forward mid-swing. In motion, it never wants to stop.

You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

Unstoppable Drive (1/Day). On your turn, you can take one additional action, as the Fighter's Action Surge feature. If you already have Action Surge, you instead gain one extra use of it. Until the end of your next turn, you ignore Difficult Terrain. This property recharges at dawn.

Once per turn. You can gain only one additional action on a given turn, whether it comes from this maul or from Action Surge itself — never both on the same turn.

When you invoke Unstoppable Drive, the maul's head hums with barely-contained kinetic force, your footfalls crack stone and packed earth, and dust shivers off nearby surfaces — momentum made manifest, and nothing on the battlefield slows you down.

A key of yellowed bone, worn smooth on a cord. The teeth are cut for a heavy bar-lock. It opens the barred doors deep in the caves — and nothing else will.

Wondrous Item, Uncommon (Requires Attunement)

A battlefield chirurgeon sold it upon retiring, swearing that in thirty years of war she never lost a patient who wore it.

While wearing this pendant, you gain the following benefits.

Life Preservation. Whenever you make a Death Saving Throw, you can change a roll of 9 or lower to a 10, turning a failed save into a successful one.

Natural Healing Boost. Whenever you roll a Hit Point Die to regain Hit Points, double the number of Hit Points it restores.

Weapon (Longbow)

A tall yew bow, its grip wrapped in sweat-darkened cord and its upper limb inlaid with a small silver kestrel in stooping flight. The wood is weathered but unwarped, and the string still holds true.

Someone kept this bow well — the limbs are oiled, the nocks unchipped, the silver bird polished by a thumb that went back to it over and over. It is a good bow, and nothing more than a good bow.

Potion, Common

You regain 2d4 + 2 Hit Points when you drink this potion.

Whatever its potency, the potion’s red liquid glimmers when agitated.

Heavy gold, a man's ring, sized for a finger that used to be fatter. The seal face is worn shallow — a merchant's mark you would need wax and good light to read — and the inside of the band is polished bright, worn there by six months of being turned against an iron cuff in the dark.

It is the ring from the portrait. Same hand, same ring.

Wondrous Item, Uncommon (Requires Attunement)

You gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class and saving throws while you wear this cloak.

Potion, Uncommon

After drinking this potion, you can take a Bonus Action to exhale fire at a target within 30 feet of yourself. The target makes a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw, taking 4d6 Fire damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. The effect ends after you exhale the fire three times or when 1 hour has passed.

This potion’s orange liquid flickers, and smoke fills the top of the container and wafts out whenever it is opened.

Weapon (Greatsword), Common

A staple of the Flaming Fist of Baldur's Gate — duty-blades quenched, their smiths swear, in the company's own forge-fire, so the steel keeps a banked heat that never quite goes out. The pawnbroker on Daggerford's market square sold it cheap; he was tired, he said, of his shop window smoldering like a hearth after dark.

In Darkness, the unsheathed blade of this weapon glows like charcoal embers, creating Bright Light in a 15-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 15 feet.

The banked heat sears where the blade bites: when you hit with an attack roll using this magic weapon, the target takes an extra 1 Fire damage.
